item.title: Scaled three-dimensional simulations of giant-planet accretion and disk clearing
item.description: arXiv:2610.15876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop accelerated three-dimensional simulations of growing planet pairs that draw on a finite gas reservoir. An annulus compression (Scaling A) shortens the predicted clearing time and shrinks the computational domain at equal grid resolution while preserving key physical parameters. Planetary seeds start with Hill radii equal to the disk scale height, retaining three-dimensional accretion. We demonstrate the method in scaled PDS 70 and Solar-System configurations, assuming perfect Hill capture by growing planets on circular orbits. We compare Scaling A at radius-compression factor \(\Gamma=1.75\) with the unscaled PDS system at matched resolution, through a 1\% reduction of the interplanetary gas inventory. The scaled run is nearly an order of magnitude faster, with similar accreted mass and a comparable partition of gas between the planets. For the Solar-System configuration at \(\Gamma=3\), the scaling forecasts a speedup of nearly two orders of magnitude at equal local resolution. The scaling is complementary to orbital advection. On eight CPU cores of a desktop computer, the scaled PDS 70 and Solar-System runs reduce the gas inventory between the orbiting planets by roughly half in less than a day. Accretion-driven orbital convergence narrows the shared feeding zone and, together with gas clearing, limits the planetary growth budget. In our scaled PDS 70 and Solar-System runs, the angular momentum carried by meridional inflow directly constrains delivery theory. These results establish a practical route to testing accretion theory against simulations at matched scaled parameters, before applying it to unscaled planetary systems.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Mosqueira

item.title: Blackbody evolution and circumstellar medium properties of broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae
item.description: arXiv:2610.16527v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Broad-lined H-rich superluminous supernovae (SLSNe II) tend to show signs of interaction, including a UV excess compared to a blackbody function. However, a quantitative analysis of the CSM configuration and the UV excess has so far not been performed for most of the literature sample. Additionally, SN 2023gpw showed signs of asymmetry in its peculiar blackbody and spectral evolution, raising the question of whether similar properties can be found in other SLSNe II. We aim to characterize the circumstellar environment of SLSNe II by searching for signs of asymmetry, quantifying the UV excess, and investigating any IR echoes produced by dust. Diversity among SLSNe II is also explored. We fit blackbody functions to the SEDs of SLSNe II to quantify the UV excess luminosity and its evolution. We use this to investigate mass-loss rates required to produce the excess through interaction. We also investigate the line profiles in SLSN II at late times and compare line velocities to the blackbody radius evolution. We examine public WISE IR images and place constraints on IR echoes. We find mass loss rates of $\sim10^{-4}$ to $\sim0.03\, \mathrm{M_\odot}$~yr$^{-1}$ when assuming all interaction luminosity emerges in the UV, i.e., conservative lower limits for the total mass loss rate. Radii calculated from line velocities in late-time spectra are mostly too large for a spherical interaction photosphere, only compatible with the blackbody radius evolution if the CSM is non-spherical with a low filling factor. This is in some cases supported by a mismatch between spectroscopic and blackbody expansion velocities. Considerable diversity is seen in the sample, probably as a result of different viewing angles and CSM masses. WISE images seem too shallow to observe IR echoes in SLSNe II beyond $z\sim0.1$, but in the nearest event, SN 2020jhm, a likely IR echo is detected, suggesting pre-existing dust.
item.dc:creator: Tuomas Kangas, Takashi Nagao, Uliana Pylypenko, Steve Schulze, Lin Yan

item.title: JWST Imaging of Edge-on Protoplanetary Disks. V. Flux Ratio Reversal and Disk-edge Structure in the Flying Saucer
item.description: arXiv:2610.17136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present near- and mid-infrared broadband imaging observations of the edge-on protoplanetary disk 2MASS J16281370-2431391, a.k.a. the 'Flying Saucer', obtained with NIRCam and MIRI on board JWST. These data are combined with archival optical and near-IR broadband imaging from HST, millimeter dust continuum emission from ALMA, and optical lightcurves from the K2 and TESS for a comprehensive multi-wavelength study. The JWST observations reveal a reversal of the flux ratio between the two reflection nebulae at near-infrared wavelengths (2-3 $\mu m$), which can be explained by a misaligned inner disk. For the first time, JWST reveals the bright lining along the disk edge at 2 and 3 $\mu m$, arising from forward scattering of background photons by dust grains near the $\tau\approx 1$ layer. By combining the dust lane thickness measured with HST and JWST, we find the dust grains up to at least $\sim$3$\mu$m are vertically mixed throughout the disk and have undergone significant growth. In addition, comparison of earlier HST/NICMOS J and K band images with those from JWST/NIRCam reveals variability in the scattered-light morphology, as well as measurable proper motion of the system with respect to the background stars, confirming that the Flying Saucer is co-moving with the young star population of $\rho$ Ophiuchi.
item.dc:creator: Jie Ma, Karl R. Stapelfeldt, Marion Villenave, Gaspard Duch\^ene, Fran\c{c}ois M\'enard, Ryo Tazaki, Youcef I. Bouarour, Greta Guidi, Laurine Martinien, Maxime Roumesy, Christophe Pinte

item.title: Graph Learning with Multiplicative Aggregation for Solar Filament Fragment Association Modeling in Full-disk H$\alpha$ Images
item.description: arXiv:2610.17291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar filaments are prominent features in H$\alpha$ observations. During their evolution, they often exhibit complex morphological and topological changes, which, due to line-of-sight projection effects, appear as fragmentation and merging. These phenomena make it difficult to reliably track solar filaments using automated methods, as the same structure may appear different over time. To address this issue, we formulate filament fragment association as a graph-based learning problem, where individual fragments are represented as nodes and candidate pairwise relationships are modeled as edges to infer whether fragments belong to the same filament. Furthermore, we propose a novel graph neural network (GNN) that incorporates multiplicative aggregation layers to enhance feature aggregation in the graph, replacing conventional additive aggregation with a multiplicative mechanism to better capture information between fragments. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves reliable performance in filament fragment association, validating the effectiveness of the graph-based formulation and the proposed multiplicative aggregation mechanism.
item.dc:creator: GaoFei Zhu, GangHua Lin, Xiao Yang, Suo Liu, Yu Liu, ZhiSheng Gao, Cheng Zeng

item.title: Non-equilibrium chemistry and radiation hydrodynamics in metal-poor and metal-rich interstellar gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.17577v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a flexible implementation of non-equilibrium chemical networks with the $\texttt{KROME}$ framework, coupled to a nonlocal variable Eddington tensor-closed radiation transport scheme ($\texttt{VETTAM}$). Our fiducial network is designed to explicitly capture the formation pathways of important molecular species such as CO, OH, and $\rm H_2O$, intermediaries like $\rm H_3^+$, and the destruction of these species through photon and cosmic-ray dissociation. We validate our scheme through benchmark tests, and demonstrate its success in 1D and 3D problems covering a broad range of metallicities ($0 \leq Z \lesssim \rm Z_{\odot}$) and densities ($n \lesssim 10^{17} \, \rm cm^{-3}$). We confirm earlier works that suggest that OH and $\rm H_2O$ are the key molecular species in dense gas ($n \gtrsim 10^{5} \, \rm cm^{-3}$) for $Z\lesssim 0.01 \rm Z_{\odot}$, dominate the cooling at these densities, and demonstrate that our scheme can reproduce their abundances with similar accuracy as dedicated static photo-dissociation region (PDR) codes. We also find that the dominant fine-structure coolant in dense ($n \gtrsim 10^3 \, \, \rm cm^{-3}$) PDRs transitions from CI to CII to OI at increasingly lower $Z$. Finally, we find that in turbulent media, rapid mixing at PDR interfaces renders the chemical species out of equilibrium, and show that this could potentially alleviate the long-standing problem of (static) PDR models producing excess CI in the diffuse ISM over UV absorption-line measurements. We conclude by presenting and comparing with alternative implementations of reduced but faster chemical networks in our scheme, discussing the problem-dependent performance-accuracy tradeoffs and future prospects.
item.dc:creator: Shyam H. Menon, Piyush Sharda, Blakesley Burkhart, Tommaso Grassi

item.title: Observational evidence of black hole event horizon from ultra-compact X-ray binaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.17618v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The event horizon is the most crucial feature that distinguishes black hole (BH) from all other objects in the universe. However, since no radiation can escape from the event horizon, its direct observational evidence remains lacking. Although both are compact objects, the event horizon leads to differences in the radiative behavior between black hole and neutron star (NS) X-ray binaries. Historically efforts to probe the existence of event horizons revealed that the BH X-ray binaries are fainter than NSs with similar orbital periods in their quiescent states. Here, we use a special class of X-ray binaries namely the ultra-compact X-ray binaries (UCXBs), to reveal the existence of the event horizon near stellar-mass black holes. In short-period UCXBs, gravitational radiation dominates the orbital angular momentum loss, allowing us to accurately determine their accretion rates. Based on five UCXBs with orbital periods shorter than 40 min, located in globular clusters, and identified accretors (NS or BH), we obtained their accretion rates. Combining their accretion rates and X-ray luminosities, we calculated the X-ray radiative efficiencies of NS and BH. The radiative efficiency of BH is about two to three orders of magnitude lower than that of NS systems, indicating the accretion energy is swallowed by the BH, thereby indirectly probe the presence of the event horizon.
item.dc:creator: Qian-Qi Ma, Wei-Min Gu, Shan-Shan Weng, Mouyuan Sun

item.title: Dynamically Coupled Three-dimensional Cloud-Chemistry in Rapidly Rotating Irradiated Atmospheres: an Application to the Compact White Dwarf-Brown Dwarf system ZTFJ0038+2030
item.description: arXiv:2610.17714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clouds and disequilibrium chemistry shape the observable properties of substellar and planetary atmospheres, and JWST time-resolved spectroscopy now enables direct tests of their three-dimensional structures. We present an update to the 3D atmospheric framework ADAM, coupling the dynamical core to a miniature kinetic chemistry scheme (mini-chem) and a saturation-relaxation tracer cloud module. Using this framework, we investigate the atmosphere of the brown dwarf orbiting the white dwarf ZTFJ0038+2030 in a 10-hour orbit. The brown dwarf receives stellar irradiation comparable to its internal heat flux, placing the atmosphere in a regime where the circulation is characterized by a standing Matsuno--Gill wave response and equatorial superrotation. Rapid rotation confines these structures closer to the equator, producing more symmetric broadband light curves with smaller hotspot offsets than canonical hot Jupiters, in agreement with recent JWST observations of this system. Although most species are globally homogenized, rapid rotation limits global-scale horizontal mixing and allows circulation-driven vertical transport to maintain strong CO and CO$_2$ inhomogeneities in the photosphere. These chemical inhomogeneities produce asymmetric phase curves in the CO and CO$_2$ absorption bands, which could qualitatively explain the observed CO$_2$ light-curve asymmetry. When clouds are included, Na$_2$S clouds dominate the photosphere and weaken the large-scale circulation, lowering photospheric CO and CO$_2$ abundances, while MgSiO$_3$ and Fe clouds rain out at deeper levels. Because the dominant Na$_2$S clouds reside mostly above the quench region, cloud-driven convection has limited impact on the quenched abundances, which are instead regulated mainly by large-scale circulation.
item.dc:creator: Yanhong Lai, Xianyu Tan, Daphne Broski-Laing, Yifan Zhou, Sarah L. Casewell, Jenni R. French, Elspeth K. H. Lee, Joshua D. Lothringer, Vivien Parmentier, Shang-Min Tsai

item.title: IC 1297: The Most Distant Known X-ray Planetary Nebula and One of the Most Luminous
item.description: arXiv:2610.17741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first targeted Einstein Probe (EP) X-ray observations of any planetary nebula (PN). Using the onboard Follow-up X-ray Telescope (FXT), we detect X-ray emission within the central region of IC 1297. The spectral analysis yields a plasma temperature of $kT = 0.086^{+0.054}_{-0.058}$ keV ($T\sim1.0 \times 10^{6}$ K), characteristic of shocked wind bubbles in PNe, whereas there is no evidence that its Wolf-Rayet central star emits X-rays. The absorption-corrected X-ray luminosity in the 0.3--2.0 keV energy band is $L_{\mathrm{X}} = 2.8 \times 10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$, also consistent with a hot bubble. At an adopted distance of $\sim3.8$ kpc, IC 1297 is the most distant X-ray emitting PN found to date, opening up a new observational window on hot-bubble formation and evolution. It is also among the most luminous known X-ray-emitting PNe. Our results demonstrate the capability of the EP FXT for detecting and characterizing faint, extended X-ray sources in the soft X-ray band for distant PNe, extending the known spectral properties of detectable X-ray emitting PNe. We also compiled the X-ray properties of all 41 known Galactic XPNe, finding a clear correlation between distance and X-ray luminosity that reflects an observational bias toward detecting the brightest sources at large distances. The compilation also shows a separation in X-ray luminosity between hot bubbles powered by H-rich and [WR]-type central stars, with the latter reaching luminosities up to an order of magnitude higher. The ten most luminous XPNe all host [WR]/PG 1159 central stars.
item.dc:creator: H. Yuan, Q. A. Parker, M. A. Guerrero

item.title: Tracing the Influence of Distant companions on Exoplanetary Systems (TIDES) I. Highly Eccentric and Misaligned Binary Companions to Hot Jupiters
item.description: arXiv:2610.17811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The origin of hot Jupiters remains an open question. A significant fraction reside in binary or multiple star systems, suggesting that stellar companions may play an important role in shaping their present-day architectures. However, the orbits of the vast majority of these stellar companions remain poorly constrained, leaving their role in hot Jupiter evolution an open question. We present the Tracing the Influence of Distant companions on Exoplanetary Systems (TIDES) survey, a campaign to map the orbits of stellar companions in systems hosting hot Jupiters to assess the extent to which binaries play a role in hot Jupiter formation and migration. Here, we introduce our survey design and new orbital fits for the first six systems in our sample---$\tau$ Boo, WASP-2, WASP-11, WASP-76, HAT-P-14, and HAT-P-16---by combining previous observations of the stellar companions together with new Keck/NIRC2 imaging and Keck/KPIC relative radial velocities. Among these six systems, the four with the most precisely constrained orbits exhibit high eccentricities ($e \geq 0.8$), and three of these systems also display significant planet--binary misalignments ($\Delta i \geq 20^\circ$). This suggests the orbital properties of stellar companions to hot Jupiter host stars are qualitatively different than field binaries and binaries hosting inner transiting small planets. These orbital architectures are consistent with stellar companions shaping the evolution of hot Jupiters, either through high-eccentricity migration or by participating in an earlier episode of dynamical evolution that ultimately led to hot Jupiter formation. Continued orbital monitoring of the full sample will reveal whether outer stellar companions play a causal role in the evolution of hot Jupiters.
item.dc:creator: Marvin Morgan, Jerry W. Xuan, Brendan P. Bowler, Kyle Franson, Michael C. Liu, Konstantin Batygin, Heather A. Knutson, Bj\"orn Benneke, Julianne Cronin, Luke Finnerty, Chih-Chun Hsu, Aniket Sanghi

item.title: Fast Radio Bursts from Monster Shocks and Flares of Inspiraling Binary Neutron Stars: A Kinetic Model for Double Pulsar
item.description: arXiv:2610.18208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The coalescence of binary neutron star systems offers unprecedented possibilities for multimessenger observations, including the detection of gravitational waves, gamma-ray bursts, kilonovae, and potentially fast radio bursts. For a detailed investigation of the latter, one requires a kinetic plasma model to describe the interacting magnetospheres of the stars. We present a three-dimensional particle-in-cell kinetic simulation of the combined magnetosphere of a binary neutron star in which the two stars physically orbit one another so that the orbital motion itself twists the magnetic loops. We find that the stellar magnetic-field intensity ratio controls the emergence of flares, while the stellar spins set the direction and modulation of the flare. We identify four spatially and dynamically distinct regions of strong electromagnetic energy release: (i) an expanding fast magnetosonic wave that steepens into a monster shock, (ii) a plasma flare being pushed by (iii) an expanding fireball and containing (iv) a reconnecting current sheet. The fast magnetosonic wave is a promising source of coherent radio emission. It is released when orbital motion cuts a closed plasma loop. The electric and magnetic wave amplitudes are similar and reach that of the background magnetic field. Our kinetic treatment yields particle spectra and plasma structures that can be used to assess coherent emission in kinetic-scale simulations. In conclusion, the stellar orbital motion constitutes a driving channel distinct from models with spin-driven magnetospheric twisting.
item.dc:creator: Jan Ben\'a\v{c}ek, Beno\^{i}t Cerutti, Martin Pohl, Tim Dietrich, Anna Neuweiler

item.title: Dynamical formation of dormant black holes: Predictions for Gaia DR4
item.description: arXiv:2610.18601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dormant black holes (dormant BHs, i.e., X-ray quiet binaries comprising a BH and a companion star) are probes of the effect of cluster dynamics and binary stellar evolution on compact-object binaries. A dozen dormant BH binaries are known, a number that will increase substantially with the upcoming Gaia Data Release 4 (DR4). Their origin is uncertain, and dynamical formation is proposed as one possible channel. Here, we study the formation of dormant BHs in low-mass star clusters, accounting for the interplay of binary stellar evolution and cluster dynamics. We present new simulations with the $N$-body code PeTar, interfaced with the population synthesis code SEVN for single and binary star evolution. Our grid spans a range of cluster masses ($300-4800\,$M$_\odot$), metallicities ($1.4\times10^{-2}$, $1.4\times10^{-4}$), and natal kick models (with and without fallback). We find that almost all dormant BH binaries escape the parent cluster within $\sim1\,$Gyr ($\sim10\,$Myr) when assuming weak (strong) natal kicks. Most ($73\%$) dormant BHs form via the exchange of a BH (or its progenitor star) into a stellar binary, or of a star into a binary with a BH. Dormant BHs in low-mass clusters have a wide orbital period distribution (from a few hours to $10^8\,$d), with an upper limit set by natal kicks, a bimodal eccentricity distribution (a first peak at zero eccentricity for circularised systems and a second at high eccentricity), and stellar masses that follow the (evolved) initial mass function. Large BH masses are a smoking gun of dynamical formation, via exchanges and stellar collisions. We expect Gaia DR4 to contain $\sim1-64$ high-metallicity and $\sim0.4-48$ low-metallicity dormant BHs, with a period distribution peaking at $\sim10^3\,$d, $\gtrsim90\%$ of them with eccentricity $e>0.1$, and $\sim20\%$ with large BH masses ($m_{\rm BH} \gtrsim 30\,$M$_\odot$).
item.dc:creator: Daniel Mar\'in Pina, Michela Mapelli, Giuliano Iorio, Cecilia Sgalletta

item.title: Peering into the Midplane of the DM Tau Disk using N2H+ and DCO+
item.description: arXiv:2610.18821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Planets form in the midplanes of protoplanetary disks, thus investigating the properties of the midplane region can shed light on the physical and chemical processes governing the evolution of planetary systems. In this work, we study the conditions near the midplane of the disk around DM Tau using 0."3 (~43 au) ALMA observations of N2H+ (J = 3 - 2) and DCO+ (J = 4 - 3). The radial profiles reveal that DCO+ is centrally peaked, with a depression near 120 au, while N2H+ exhibits a central depression and a peak near 100 au. In addition, both molecules display extended emission out to 400 au. Using parametric models to interpret our observations, we note that a fiducial model based on CO-derived parameters captures the features within 200 au, but fails to reproduce the outer disk emission. We explore various mechanisms that could account for this extended emission and conclude that it is best reproduced by an increased external UV penetration and cosmic ray/X-ray ionization rate, possibly enhanced by radial drift. These processes affect the precursors of N2H+ and DCO+ : increased UV leads to the photodesorption of CO and N2, while ionization enhances H3+ abundance. Besides, the observed N2H+ and DCO+ features are broadly consistent with previous CO snowline constraints, but can also be shaped by processes such as ionization, CO depletion, and multiple chemical pathways. Thus, using these molecular ions as robust CO snowline tracers requires additional constraints from complementary molecular tracers and detailed chemical modeling.

item.title: X-ray spectroscopy method of white dwarf mass determination in intermediate polars. External systematic uncertainties
item.description: arXiv:2506.03711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The masses of white dwarfs (WDs) in intermediate polars (IPs) can be determined from the shape of their hard X-ray spectra. Here we study the importance of all possible systematic uncertainties in this X-ray spectroscopy method, including finite radii and rotation of magnetospheres, finite accretion column height and accretion-flow inclination relative to the WD surface. We also investigate the importance of accretion-heated envelopes on WD surfaces in IPs which are increasing WD radii. Their presence changes the commonly used mass-radius relation for cold white dwarfs. As a first approximation we use thick ($10^{-4}M_\odot$) hydrogen envelope models with a surface temperature of 30 kK. We present a new model grid of hard X-ray spectra of high-luminous IPs computed among other things with using a new mass-radius relation. This grid is used for fitting Swift/BAT spectra of 47 IPs. The average WD mass in this sample is 0.82 $M_\odot$ and coincides with the average WD mass in cataclysmic variables obtained by optical methods. This means that the calculated hard X-ray spectra and the assumptions made that the magnetospheric radii in IPs are close to the corotation radii, and the relative heights of the accretion columns are small are basically correct, because most IPs have high luminosities. But this universal grid (as well as previous universal grids) cannot give correct results for the low-luminous IPs with probably relatively tall accretion columns on the WD surfaces. Such IPs have to be investigated with individual accretion column models.

item.title: Nonlocal Evolution of Magnetic Helicity across the Magnetohydrodynamic-Kinetic Interface
item.description: arXiv:2507.13213v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic helicity is typically indistinguishable from noise in the solar wind inertial range. Using Parker Solar Probe measurements (0.1-0.8 au), we report a robust bihelical structure emerging at the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD)-kinetic interface. This structure, formed by a striking pair of positive and negative peaks, exhibits a systematic spectral migration toward lower frequencies with increasing heliocentric distance. Crucially, this evolution deviates from local kinetic scaling laws, such as the radial decline of the ion cyclotron frequency, reflecting a nonlocal evolution of magnetic topology. Our findings provide a new observational constraint on both nonlocal MHD transport processes and the nature of the helicity barrier in the kinetic regime.
item.dc:creator: Masatomi Iizawa, Yasuhito Narita, Tommaso Alberti, Stuart D. Bale, Axel Brandenburg, Abraham C. -L. Chian, Horia Comi\c{s}el, Shuichi Matsukiyo, Nobumitsu Yokoi

item.title: Chemical transport by weakly nonlinear internal gravity waves in stars
item.description: arXiv:2510.02031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While internal gravity waves (IGWs) are known to transport chemicals in the radiative zones of stars, substantial uncertainty remains regarding the magnitude and physical mechanisms of this transport. Most previous studies have relied on heuristic theories or numerical simulations that are difficult to extrapolate to stellar parameters. In this work, we present the first rigorous asymptotic calculation of (passive) chemical transport by IGWs, in the limit of small wave amplitude. The net vertical transport induced by a coherent packet of waves is found to be proportional to the horizontal mean of $(w^S+w^E)^2$, where $w^S$ and $w^E$ are the vertical Stokes and Eulerian mean velocities. The transport scales as the fourth power of wave amplitude and quadratically with time, and we verify these scalings with numerical simulations. In the weakly damped regime, the dominant transport coefficients scale as $\omega^{-2}\kappa^2$, where $\omega$ is the wave frequency and $\kappa$ is the radiative diffusivity. Because the transport can be positive or negative depending on the wave phases, the effective mixing induced by the superposition of coherent wave packets is expected to scale with the eighth power of wave amplitude. These results provide a theoretical foundation for making accurate predictions of IGW-induced chemical transport in stellar evolution models.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Mao, Daniel Lecoanet

item.title: On the center-to-limb variations of the He I 10830 \AA\ triplet
item.description: arXiv:2511.14331v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present high-resolution spectroscopic observations of the quiet-Sun center-to-limb variations (CLV) of the He I triplet at 10830 {\AA} and the nearby Si I 10827 {\AA} line, observed with GREGOR Infrared Spectrograph (GRIS) and the improved High-resolution Fast Imager (HiFI+). The observations cover the interval $\mu = [0.1,\, 1.0]$, where $\mu$ is the cosine of the heliocentric angle. At each $\mu$-position, the spectra are spatially averaged over 0.02 $\mu$, and the resulting CLVs are given both as these averaged data points and as smooth polynomial curves fitted across each wavelength point. The He I spectra were inverted using the HAnle and ZEeman Light (HAZEL) code, showing an increase in optical depth towards the limb and a reversed convective blueshift for the red component, while the blue component was entirely absent. In addition, we find a strong increase in the steepness of the He I CLV compared to that of the nearby continuum. The Si I showed a behavior more typical of photospheric lines, namely shallower CLV, a reduction in width and depth, and a more typical convective blueshift.
item.dc:creator: A. G. M. Pietrow, C. Kuckein, M. Verma, C. Denker, J. C. Trelles Arjona, R. Kamlah, K. Poppenh\"ager

item.title: A rotational line CO cooling rate prescription for AGB outflows
item.description: arXiv:2602.12777v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars significantly contribute to the chemical composition of the universe. In their outflows, complex chemistry takes place, which critically depends on the local temperature. Therefore, if we want to accurately model the AGB environment, we need accurate cooling rates. The CO molecule is abundant in AGB outflows, and has a dipole moment, which enables it to cool through emission from its rotational transitions. We therefore expect it to significantly contribute to cooling in this environment, even at low temperatures ($10$ K $\leqslant T\leqslant 3000$ K). Currently, CO cooling rates are available for ISM-like conditions, which encompasses a different parameter regime, with generally lower densities and velocity gradients, compared to AGB winds. Therefore, these ISM cooling rates might not be applicable to the AGB regime. In this paper, we compute CO cooling rates for hydrodynamics simulations of AGB outflows. To evaluate the net cooling rate, we calculate the energy level distribution of CO self-consistently, using the non Local Thermodynamical Equilibrium (NLTE) line radiative transfer code Magritte. We verify whether already existing CO cooling rate prescriptions for the interstellar medium (ISM) are applicable for this regime. We noticed minor differences between these prescriptions and our calculated cooling rates in general. However, when used far outside their originally intended parameter regimes, significant differences occur. Therefore, we propose a new CO cooling rate prescription for the AGB environment and we study how the computed cooling rate varies depending on input parameters.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: RAS Techniques and Instruments, Volume 5, 2026, rzag009
item.dc:creator: T. Ceulemans, F. De Ceuster, O. Vermeulen, L. Decin

item.title: The $R$-Process Alliance: Actinide Abundances, Variation, and Evolution in Metal-Poor Stars
item.description: arXiv:2604.12892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The actinides, including thorium (Th), are the heaviest observable elements synthesized in the universe, holding clues to the extremes of the astrophysical and nuclear conditions of $r$-process sites. We present Th abundances based on high-resolution spectroscopy for 47 metal-poor stars, the largest homogeneously analyzed sample to date. The chemical evolution of Th exhibits a decrease in dispersion in [Th/H] and [Th/Fe] from $\sim$0.6 dex at the lowest metallicities to $\sim$0.2 dex at higher metallicities. We also find that Th and the lanthanides Eu and Dy are co-produced remarkably well, with average [Th/Eu]$\sim0.0$ across $-3.0 \lesssim$ [Fe/H] $\lesssim -1.5$, as well as across stars with $0.0\lesssim$ [Eu/Fe] $\lesssim2.5$. Even so, the absolute range of $\log\epsilon$(Th/Eu) is 1.02 dex, with an observed standard deviation of $\pm0.20$ dex and an intrinsic standard deviation of $\pm0.11$ dex at the lowest metallicities. We infer that $68\%$ of $r$-process events have $\log\epsilon$(Th/Eu) yields that only vary within a factor of $\pm1.3$ or $\pm30\%$, while $5\%$ of $r$-process events have $\log\epsilon$(Th/Eu) yields that vary by factors $>3.3$ approaching $\sim$10. This serves as a strong constraint for the nuclear and astrophysical models of $r$-process sites, and suggests that achieving an $r$-process site that is both prompt and produces a robust $\log\epsilon$(Th/Eu) ratio is a challenge for current models.

item.title: Asymmetric nightside CO2 features, inefficient heat transport, and precise evolutionary constraints: Spectroscopic phase curves reveal the past and present of a white dwarf-brown dwarf binary
item.description: arXiv:2606.30112v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first JWST phase curve of a white dwarf-brown dwarf binary, a NIRSpec PRISM observation of ZTFJ0038+2030. Short-period white dwarf-brown dwarf binaries provide unique laboratories to probe substellar atmospheres. Tidal locking drives hot Jupiter-like atmospheric dynamics in the brown dwarf. The system's formation history offers a window into planetary systems around post-main-sequence stars. We obtain a full-orbit phase curve of ZTF0038, including a total eclipse of the white dwarf, which enables us to separate the two components' emission throughout the entire orbit, and we model the brown dwarf's phase-resolved emission spectra using substellar atmosphere forward models and atmospheric retrievals. The PRISM spectrum covers ~80% of the brown dwarf's bolometric emission, enabling a nearly model-independent energy balance calculation, which yields a day-to-nightside heat transport efficiency of <10%. Inefficient heat redistribution is further supported by the phase curve shape and the nightside spectrum closely resembling non-irradiated mid-to-late T dwarfs. The spectroscopic phase curves reveal a stark nightside asymmetry associated with a strong CO2 absorption feature at 4.2 um, while the retrieved abundances indicate a longitudinally homogeneous distribution of CO2 as well as all other key species detected in the atmosphere. The precise internal luminosity measurement of the brown dwarf informs both the age of the WD-BD system (7.5-8.8 Gyr) and indicates a low common-envelope ejection efficiency. These data illustrate the exquisite opportunity to probe the three-dimensional processes of substellar atmospheres, connect substellar and exoplanet atmospheres, and probe the evolution of post-main-sequence planetary systems using WD-BDs.

item.title: Collisionless and collisional kinetics of a plasma atmosphere with spatially and temporally intermittent heating at its base
item.description: arXiv:2607.08410v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The solar corona exhibits a pronounced temperature inversion, with plasma temperatures increasing by nearly two orders of magnitude from the chromosphere to the corona. We investigate how spatially sparse and temporally intermittent stochastic heating at the base of the transition region shapes the temperature and density structure of coronal loops within a kinetic framework. Stochastic thermal boundary conditions and surface coarse graining are introduced. Analytical solutions are derived in the collisionless limit for heating-event time scales shorter or longer than the particle crossing time, and Coulomb collisions are incorporated through a reduced kinetic model describing the thermalization of suprathermal particles. In the short-time-scale regime, spatial filling factor and temporal intermittency combine into a single effective parameter controlling the suprathermal population, producing a transition region and a hot corona both within individual loops and after coarse graining. Collisions preserve this thermal structure while reducing the coronal density through progressive thermalization. In the long-time-scale regime, individual loops are nearly isothermal and the temperature inversion emerges only after coarse graining, depending solely on the spatial filling factor. Here, Coulomb collisions and optically thin radiative losses have only minor effects, while density and temperature profiles remain broadly consistent with coronal observations. These results show that sparse, intermittent heating naturally generates suprathermal particle distributions and reproduces the observed thermal structure of the solar corona within a kinetic framework, highlighting the different sensitivity of the two regimes to collisional effects.

item.title: A multi-source dataset for solar energetic particle forecasting
item.description: arXiv:2607.16160v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solar energetic particle (SEP) event forecasting often involves integrating heterogeneous observations that differ in cadence, temporal coverage, format, and historical availability, posing challenges for reproducible analysis of data-driven approaches. This paper presents SEP-PRISM Data, a curated multi-source dataset designed for 24-hour-ahead forecasting of operational SEP events, defined as proton flux exceeding 10 pfu in the GOES > 10 MeV channel. SEP-PRISM Data integrates flare records, active-region magnetic field parameters, coronal mass ejection (CME) catalog data, GOES soft X-ray flux, and historical proton flux into a common window-based representation spanning 3 February 1986 to 10 September 2025. To improve temporal coverage and cross-source consistency, SHARP and SMARP magnetic products were aligned into a unified SMHARP archive, and CME records from DONKI and CDAW were aligned into a unified CDAWDONKI event set. Predictor variables were summarized over fixed non-overlapping 24-hour historical windows using minimum, mean, and maximum statistics and paired with targets defined over the subsequent 24-hour window, forming a supervised learning dataset. The resulting SEP-PRISM Data contains 14,464 labeled samples, including 650 positive operational SEP cases, and is intended to support reproducible benchmarking, model development, feature analysis, and future studies of space weather forecasting.

item.title: The Nineteenth Data Release of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey
item.description: arXiv:2507.07093v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mapping the local and distant Universe is key to our understanding of it. For decades, the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) has made a concerted effort to map millions of celestial objects to constrain the physical processes that govern our Universe. The most recent and fifth generation of SDSS (SDSS-V) is organized into three scientific ``mappers". Milky Way Mapper (MWM) that aims to chart the various components of the Milky Way and constrain its formation and assembly, Black Hole Mapper (BHM), which focuses on understanding supermassive black holes in distant galaxies across the Universe, and Local Volume Mapper (LVM), which uses integral field spectroscopy to map the ionized interstellar medium in the local group. This paper describes and outlines the scope and content for the nineteenth data release (DR19) of SDSS and the most substantial to date in SDSS-V. DR19 is the first to contain data from all three mappers. Additionally, we also describe nine value added catalogs (VACs) that enhance the science that can be conducted with the SDSS-V data. Finally, we discuss how to access SDSS DR19 and provide illustrative examples and tutorials.

item.title: A Unified Charge-Dependent Modulation Model for AMS-02 Proton and Antiproton Fluxes during Solar Minimum
item.description: arXiv:2601.07649v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a unified charge-dependent solar modulation model by solving the three-dimensional Parker transport equation, incorporating a realistic wavy heliospheric current sheet to treat drift effects self-consistently. Using a local interstellar spectrum from GALPROP constrained by Voyager data, we fit the model to time-resolved proton and antiproton fluxes measured by the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer-02 (AMS-02) from May 2011 to June 2022, excluding the heliospheric magnetic field (HMF) polarity-reversal epoch (mid-2012 to early 2015). To enable rapid parameter scans, we employ neural-network-based surrogate models to compute propagation and modulation matrices efficiently. The results demonstrate that the model simultaneously describes the observed proton and antiproton fluxes with physically reasonable parameters, providing a unified account of charge-dependent modulation.

item.title: Circumbinary Discs as the Origin of Circumstellar Material around Interacting H-poor Supernovae and Fast Blue Optical Transients
item.description: arXiv:2604.20035v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Around 10 % of hydrogen-poor supernovae explode inside compact ($\sim 10^{15}$ cm), massive ($\sim 0.1 \ \mathrm{M_\odot}$) circumstellar material (CSM), signalling an episode of enhanced pre-explosion mass loss whose mechanism remains unclear. The extreme members of this population are considered to constitute some of the Fast Blue Optical Transients (FBOTs), which exhibit rapid rise times of $\sim$ few days and high peak luminosity $\sim 10^{44} \ \mathrm{erg}$. Recent binary evolution calculations show that the expansion of helium stars during their latest evolutionary stages can trigger a rapid but stable mass-transfer episode that can form a dense circumbinary disc (CBD) that may explain the observed dense CSM. However, a detailed, quantitative analysis of this process and the resulting CBD properties such as its mass, radius and density profile has not yet been undertaken. We present a set of models that solve the viscous evolution of such a CBD under time-dependent mass injection. We find that although the injected mass is initially sub-Keplerian, a lower ``accretion eigenvalue'' $\chi$ prevents more mass from falling back onto the central binary. For our fiducial set of models, the CBD immediately prior to the explosion reaches a mass of $0.07-0.20 \ \mathrm{M}_\odot$, a half-mass radius of $640 - 4000 \ \mathrm{R}_\odot$, and an aspect ratio of $\theta = H/R \sim 0.1$. We also show that the interaction between SN ejecta and the CBD can power some of the fastest-evolving interacting Type Ibc SNe that can be classified as FBOTs, such as SN 2018gep or SN 2019jc. Despite uncertainties in the model parameters, our results demonstrate that CBD formation triggered by rapid, stable mass transfer is a viable mechanism to explain the dense circumstellar environments observed around rapid, hydrogen-poor interacting SNe. item.title: CausticFlow: An Efficient Machine Learning Framework Combining Neural Differential Equations and Normalizing Flows for Binary Microlensing Parameter Inference
item.description: arXiv:2607.04955v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce CausticFlow, a machine learning framework that combines neural controlled differential equations with normalizing flows to infer binary microlensing parameters. This architecture naturally handles irregularly sampled time series and data gaps while flexibly capturing strongly correlated and multimodal posterior distributions. Trained on simulated KMTNet-like light curves, CausticFlow generates posterior samples in a fraction of a second, with maximum-a-posteriori estimates achieving typical precisions of $\sim17\%$ for the mass ratio $q$ and $\sim3\%$ for the projected separation $s$. When used as a proposal distribution for downstream local optimization, the framework improves these precisions to $<5\%$ and $<1\%$, respectively, and recovers model $\chi^2$ for $\sim80\%$ of simulated events. We test the generalizability of the framework on 10 real binary lensing events characterized by higher-order effects, varied cadences, and real-world noise. Despite these mismatches between simulation and reality, CausticFlow successfully recovers the model parameters, light-curve morphology, and lensing geometry for 7 of the 10 events after simple local refinement, achieving precision levels comparable to those found for simulated data in 10 CPU minutes per event. These results demonstrate that CausticFlow acts as a fast and robust proposal engine that provides informative starting points for downstream local optimization, bridging the gap between the rapid influx of data and the need for systematic modeling in large-scale microlensing surveys such as Roman, CSST, and ET.

item.title: An Adaptive Approach for Modeling Collisionless Plasma Shocks and Ion Heating in the Shock Frame
item.description: arXiv:2608.00253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a novel computational method for hybrid (kinetic ions, quasi-neutral fluid electrons) simulations of non-relativistic magnetized collisionless plasma shocks, observed near the Sun, in the solar system, and beyond. This Adaptive Frame-Of-Reference Approach (AFORA) enables simulations of shocks in their co-moving frames of reference, where shock evolution remains quasi-steady for quasi-stationary upstream conditions, in contrast to moving shocks. We demonstrate our method in two spatial dimensions for a range of angles between the background magnetic field and the shock normal (obliquities). Shock-frame simulations, conducted with a time-adaptive hybrid code, HYPERS, are shown to self-consistently capture upstream and downstream magnetic fluctuations commonly observed by spacecraft at interplanetary shocks and Earth's bow shock. These fluctuations, which may be crucial for estimating the efficiency of ion acceleration at heliospheric and astrophysical shocks, are notably missing from many hybrid simulations of shocks, unless upstream external turbulence is imposed. The quasi-stationary behavior of numerical shocks in the shock frame is confirmed in a series of animations and by demonstrating converged ion energy spectra in the downstream region. Our approach underscores computationally efficient and physically more accurate modeling of shock-driven turbulence, downstream plasma relaxation, and concomitant ion heating in the shock frame. The new method can be used for exploring ion relaxation at interplanetary (IP) shocks, more efficient studies of cosmic rays (CRs) and plasma turbulence, and more accurate predictions of seed populations of Solar Energetic Particles (SEPs) at heliospheric shocks driven by coronal mass ejections (CMEs).

item.title: Confining density functional approach to the QCD phase diagram at low temperatures and thermal twin stars
item.description: arXiv:2608.18038v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a density functional-based equation of state for warm, dense nuclear matter with a transition to deconfined quark matter for applications to simulations of supernova explosions and neutron star mergers, but also for the cosmological evolution of Q-balls. For the quark matter equation of state, we employ a recently developed confining density functional approach while nuclear matter is described within a relativistic density functional model of the DD2 class. The phase transition is obtained by a Maxwell construction at constant entropy per baryon. We discuss the solutions of TOV equations for isentropic hybrid stars for two hybrid equation of state models: DDf-SFM without and DD2-$\chi$CDF with color superconductivity. We find that at finite temperatures above a critical value of entropy per baryon sequences of disconnected third family branches ("thermal twin stars") may appear for the DDf-SFM model, while they are absent for the color superconducting model and at $T=0$. We discuss the relation of this critical entropy per baryon to the Seidov criterion of gravitational instability for $T=0$ and find that it is a good guide. We suggest that the presence of thermal twin stars may be regarded as an indicator for the core-collapse supernova explodability of massive blue supergiant stars with solar metallicity and thus serve as a new criterion for the reliability of hybrid equation of state models. By this argument, strong color superconductivity shall be excluded and it remains to be shown whether models with moderate diquark pairing could fulfill the thermal twin constraint. For the case of symmetric matter, we compare the resulting hybrid EOS with the flow constraint by Danielewicz et al. and find a a sensitivity of the onset density for deconfinement to the presence or absence of color superconductivity.

item.title: The First Multi-Messenger Nova: External Shocks, TeV Photons, and Neutrinos in the Next Eruption of T CrB
item.description: arXiv:2609.06201v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: T Coronae Borealis is the most compelling anticipated Galactic recurrent nova and one of the best opportunities to test whether nova eruptions can become genuine multi-messenger transients. Recent observational work on classical novae has shown that the GeV $\gamma$-ray luminosity correlates strongly with the differential velocity between interacting outflows, suggesting that shock power depends strongly on velocity contrast. We apply this empirical framework to T CrB and compare it with the 2021 eruption of RS Ophiuchi, the only nova securely detected at TeV energies. We argue that T CrB may lie at the extreme high-$\Delta v$ end of the nova population and that its strongest shock should arise at the external interaction between the nova ejecta and the slow circumbinary medium. This makes the external shock the most likely site of any TeV emission, while the GeV signal may contain contributions from both internal, if present, and external shocks. Because T CrB is substantially closer than RS Oph, it is an especially favorable target for TeV detection. The neutrino case is promising but more uncertain because it depends sensitively on the density and structure of the circumbinary material. We also revisit the recurrence time of T CrB. Using the observed scatter of better-sampled recurrent novae, we infer a representative population-scale recurrence of $T_{\rm rec}\simeq80\pm12$ yr. Taken together, its proximity and potentially extreme shock velocities make T CrB perhaps the best opportunity for a nova to become the first securely established multi-messenger nova.

item.title: How dust particles orbiting white dwarfs can reveal undetected co-orbiting exoplanets II. Exoplanets on elliptic orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.04358v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Abridged. We aim to extend Paper I to the eccentric secondary orbit case and now analyse the elliptic restricted three-body problem (ERTBP). Our secondary masses include Ceres, Mercury, Earth, and Neptune so that we can help infer the presence of both large asteroids and planets through our analysis. We study dust particles on both planar (2D-ERTBP) and non-coplanar (3D-ERTBP) orbits. We computed families of 1/1 resonant symmetric and asymmetric periodic orbits in the 2D-ERTBP and 3D-ERTBP. Doing so produces novel results in their own right and diagnostic tools for precise guidance for our next steps. Based on them, we generated detailed phase portraits. Finally, we run suitably seeded $N$-body simulations to compare with the periodic orbits, and to provide observational links with debris close to WDs. New families of asymmetric periodic orbits, called $E^A_{41}$, $E^A_{42}$, and $E^A_{43}$ in the high-eccentricity 2D-ERTBP regime were discovered. They are generated by the new bifurcation point, $B_T^4$, along the new $A_2$ family, showcased in Paper I. Moreover, new isolated families of asymmetric periodic orbits, namely $E^A_{44}$, $E^A_{45}$, and $E^A_{46}$ were discovered. Families of short- and long- period asymmetric orbits starting from $L_4$, called $E^A_S$ and $E^A_L$, were also computed. In both the 2D- and 3D-ERTBP regimes, highly eccentric motion is exhibited for the dust particles in the majority of the families of either symmetric or asymmetric periodic orbits. The $N$-body simulations reveal that over ten years, the orbital period deviations of the dust are higher than in the circular restricted three-body problem (Paper I); in some architectures, Mercury-mass planets can regularly generate deviations exceeding $\sim$100 s, which potentially aids observational inferences of hidden asteroids or planets orbiting WDs.

item.title: OGLE-2016-BLG-0523: A Low-mass Brown Dwarf or super-Jupiter in a $>100$ au Orbit
item.description: arXiv:2610.13942v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To search for very wide-orbit binary-lens events, we cross-match microlensing events detected by OGLE-IV and KMTNet between 2011 and 2024. After removing contaminants from variable stars, we identify OGLE-2016-BLG-0523 as a microlensing event showing two short-lived bumps in its light curve, with the two separated by 8.36 yr. We investigate three scenarios to explain the two bumps, including a binary-lens single-source (2L1S), a single-lens binary-source (1L2S), and two unrelated single-lens single-source events (2$\times$1L1S). The 1L2S interpretation is excluded due to its poorer fit to the data, while the 2$\times$1L1S scenario is disfavored by the low event rate, unphysical total source flux, and unphysical color for one of the two putative sources. For the surviving 2L1S interpretation, the Einstein timescales of the two bumps are $8.343 \pm 0.076$ days and $3.231 \pm 0.047$ days, respectively, implying a binary mass ratio of $q = 0.15$. A Bayesian analysis indicates that the primary lens is most likely a low-mass M dwarf, while the companion is probably a low-mass brown dwarf or super-Jupiter. The inferred projected separation is about 450 au, making the companion the widest low-mass object discovered via microlensing to date. Our discovery highlights both the promise and challenges of identifying very wide, low-mass companions through microlensing. Although upcoming facilities such as Roman and Earth 2.0 space telescopes will improve sensitivity to such events, overcoming degeneracies and distinguishing them from variable phenomena will remain essential for building a robust statistical sample.
